intro: The subjunctive starts from the «yo» form; six verbs have their own forms.
p.tener.consejo: From «tengo» comes «tenga, tengas, tenga…»: the g of the «yo» form passes to the whole subjunctive.
p.hacer.consejo: «Hago» gives «haga, hagas…». The c of the infinitive disappears: now it is a g.
p.decir.consejo: «Digo» gives «diga, digas…». The e of «decir» becomes i and a g appears.
p.salir.consejo: «Salgo» gives «salga, salgas…». It is the same g that «tener» and «venir» have.
p.ir.consejo: It does not follow the «yo» form: «voy» but «vaya, vayas». It is one of the six rebels.
p.ser.consejo: Another rebel: «soy» but «sea, seas». You have to memorise it.
p.saber.consejo: «Sé» but «sepa, sepas». With a clear p; it does not look like «sabe».
p.dar.consejo: «Dé» has an accent so it is not confused with «de». The others: «des, dé, demos, deis, den».
p.conocer.consejo: «Conozco» gives «conozca, conozcas…». The c sounds like th: «ko-NOTH-ka».
p.médico.consejo: It has an accent on the first e. For a woman: «la médica».
p.grave.consejo: It works for a man and a woman. If something «no es grave», there is no need to worry.
p.razón.consejo: «Tener razón» means being correct. In English you say «to be right».
b1.texto:
For the subjunctive, take the **yo** form of the present, drop the **-o** and add the opposite vowel:

- **-ar** → e, es, e, emos, éis, en
- **-er / -ir** → a, as, a, amos, áis, an

So an irregular «yo» passes to the whole tense: tengo → **tenga**, hago → **haga**, digo → **diga**, salgo → **salga**, conozco → **conozca**.

Only six verbs have their own form: ser → **sea**, ir → **vaya**, estar → **esté**, haber → **haya**, saber → **sepa**, dar → **dé**.
b2.f0.texto: I want you to go to the doctor.
b2.f1.texto: I don't think it is anything serious.
b2.f3.texto: But I want your sister to know it.
b2.f4.texto: Do you want me to tell your sister anything?
b2.f5.texto: Tell her to come tomorrow and to stay calm.
b2.f6.texto: Tomorrow I leave work and go with her.
b2.f7.texto: Thanks, I hope everything goes well.
b4.texto:
There are three groups to know:

- **They come from «yo»**: tengo → tenga · hago → haga · digo → diga · salgo → salga · conozco → conozca · vengo → venga.
- **Six rebels**: ser → sea · ir → vaya · estar → esté · haber → haya · saber → sepa · dar → dé.
- **They change the vowel**: quiero → quiera · puedo → pueda · duermo → duerma, but in «nosotros» and «vosotros»: queramos, podamos, **durmamos**.

Spelling keeps the sound: busco → bus**que**, llego → lle**gue**, empiezo → empie**ce**.

A trick: learn the «tú» form of each verb and the other persons follow.
b4.e0.texto: I want you to leave the house early.
b4.e1.texto: I want you to meet my family.
b4.e2.texto: I want you to give me your number.
b5.f0.texto: The waiting room smells of soap and camomile.
b5.f1.texto: A big clock marks the minutes with a dry tick.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía flicks through an old magazine with cold hands.
b5.f3.texto: An elderly woman with white hair smiles from the corner.
b5.f4.texto: The afternoon light falls on the tiled floor.
b5.f5.texto: At last a nurse opens the white door.
b5.f6.texto: She says Lucía's name in a calm voice.
b5.f7.texto: The doctor, a tall man with kind eyes, greets her from his desk.
b5.f8.texto: He listens patiently to her cough and writes some words on a paper.
b5.f9.texto: On leaving, Lucía breathes deeply under the grey sky.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Ir» is a rebel: vaya, vayas, vaya.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Vas» is the ordinary present, with no wish.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Ibas» is the imperfect past, a different tense.
b6.pregunta: What is the subjunctive of «ir» for tú?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Haces» is the ordinary present. After a wish comes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive only works with a single subject.
b7.pregunta: You ask Pablo to do it. Which form is missing?
b8.traduccion: Do you want me to tell her anything?
b9.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «Sé» but «sepa»: its own form.
b9.pregunta: Which verb does NOT come from the «yo» form?
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Sale» is the ordinary present, with no wish.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work: here the subject changes.
b10.pregunta: You hope all goes well. Which form is missing?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I want you to know» (tú).
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Das» is the ordinary present. Here you need the subjunctive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Dar» is a rebel: des (and «dé» with an accent for él).
b12.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work when another person acts.
b12.pregunta: You ask for a phone number. Which form is missing?
p.vayas.consejo: Subjunctive of «ir» for tú. It is irregular: it does not come from «voy». The v sounds b.
p.tengas.consejo: Subjunctive of «tener» for tú. It comes from «tengo»: the g stays.
p.sepa.consejo: Subjunctive of «saber» for yo, él or usted. It is one of the six irregular ones.
p.esté.consejo: Subjunctive of «estar» for yo, él or usted. The accent separates it from «este» (this).
p.salgas.consejo: Subjunctive of «salir» for tú. It comes from «salgo»: «salgo» → «salgas».
p.conozcas.consejo: Subjunctive of «conocer» for tú. It comes from «conozco»: the c and z sound th.
p.des.consejo: Subjunctive of «dar» for tú. It has no accent. «Dé» (él) has one so it is not «de».
p.hojea.consejo: From «hoja» (page): to turn the pages quickly. The h is silent and the j sounds h.
p.anciana.consejo: The c sounds th: «an-THYA-na». The masculine is «anciano». It is a respectful word.
p.baldosas.consejo: The singular is «baldosa». You say «suelo de baldosas» for a floor covered with tiles.
p.hagas.consejo: Subjunctive of «hacer» for tú. It comes from «hago»; the h is silent: «A-gas».
